source_text: In contrast, male circumcision removes the foreskin (with fewer nerve endings and partial sensory role) and, when voluntary and hygienic, reduces heterosexual HIV acquisition by 60% per randomized trials, alongside lower UTI and penile cancer rates, rendering it non-equivalent in harm-benefit calculus.
